ask: Should an edit made during a review send the passage back for review?
problem: A recorder can add a second version to a passage with audio, even mid-review. Nobody is asked to listen, and the passage still looks finished.
found: I tried neither phone nor web; both failed here. From the code: the new version goes live, old checks still count, and the passage stays Done. Partner apps keep the last approved version.
changed: Nothing yet. I built nothing, as you asked.
why: Earlier decisions say publishing never sends anything by itself, and only approved versions leave the team. Option 2 fits both: it shows the gap and leaves sending to the recorder.
touches: Option 2 changes the Done label and one message on the passage. Option 3 breaks an earlier decision. Option 4 adds a choice to publishing.

options.label: Keep it as it is
options.result: Edits never go back for review. Unheard audio can hide behind a Done passage.

options.label: Mark it, and offer to send
options.result: The passage says the new version is not checked. The main button offers Send to the usual reviewer. Nothing is sent by itself.

options.label: Send it back automatically
options.result: Every edit after a check goes to the reviewer at once. Nothing slips through, but small fixes bother reviewers.

options.label: Ask the editor when they publish
options.result: Publishing shows two buttons: send for review, or publish only. The editor decides each time.
